A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same Boundary Guidance study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained experiments across the revised structure.

before.justification: v1 reports original Qwen2.5 and Gemma fine-tuning experiments, helpfulness and harmfulness measurements, and reward ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds long-context, alternative-classifier, prompt-subgroup, and alternative-judge evaluations.

M1.justification: The reported main reward changes from u+t above the threshold and u−t below it (v1 Equation 3) to u+|t−0.5| (v2 Equation 1). This removes a unit discontinuity and changes relative incentives for safe versus unsafe completions. The guard-only rewrite is equivalent up to an additive constant. Retained numerical results do not establish that training was rerun.

E1.justification: v2 adds HotpotQA multi-document question answering as a longer-context scenario in a targeted Qwen2.5-7B experiment (Section 5.2.3). The original jailbreak, Alpaca, and HarmfulQA coverage remains the principal experimental setting.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain the corresponding instruction-tuned base generators within filtered systems. ShieldGemma and Granite Guardian are alternative components tested in guard ablations; no additional competing fine-tuning algorithm is evaluated.

E3.justification: New experiments vary previously fixed conditions: Qwen2.5-7B training with 1,970 HotpotQA prompts selected using a 1,000-word limit, guard substitution with ShieldGemma-2B and Granite-Guardian-HAP-125M, and evaluation with Gemini 2.5 Flash without thinking. The original tabulated training budgets and evaluation score scales remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial tests of training-context composition, classifier strength, judge dependence, and differences between prompt categories (Sections 5.2.3–5.2.4 and Appendices C–D). These investigate previously untested limits of aggregate improvements. The original reward ablations and failure examples are retained, with the latter moved from Appendix C to E.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 newly discloses that results use a single training run and describes variability as arising from evaluation data. This clarifies the scope of uncertainty without establishing additional runs. Paired t-tests and the existing significance thresholds are retained.

E6.justification: Original aggregate entries in Tables 1–3 and filtered-response counts are retained, while substantial subgroup, long-context, weaker-guard, and Gemini results are added. Under Gemini judging, Qwen2.5-7B helpfulness is 2.79 versus 3.03 for its base model (Table 9). v2 also correctly attributes the existing −0.73 guard-only helpfulness collapse to Qwen2.5-0.5B; v1's prose incorrectly named 7B.

T1.justification: v1's calibrated-probability utility model and constant-helpfulness special case are replaced by general score-conditioned passing and rejection utilities. v2 adds an optimal-threshold global-minimum theorem and a proposition with a derivative proof establishing sufficient monotonicity conditions. This substantially revises the mathematical foundation.

C1.justification: The central boundary-avoidance contribution remains. The abstract extends coverage to long-context prompts, while the introduction and Figure 2 qualify improvements as occurring in most settings. The conclusion additionally claims Pareto improvements across guard models, although Table 5 reports helpfulness losses with both alternative guards.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning prompt-mix dependence, judge sensitivity, insufficient classifier capability, possible reward-model distillation, and longer-context training instability. Limitations now connect success to score monotonicity and confidently wrong classifications. Future work adds deployment-filter changes, while the earlier welfare-filter proposal is removed.

D1.justification: v2 adds the TRL implementation reference, a no-scaling disclosure, explicit scoring treatment of filtered outputs, and details for new experiments. It removes v1's explicit 1,000-question balanced test-set description and KL-regularization statements without establishing actual setting changes. The hyperparameter table, hardware information, and repository link remain.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands positioning against classifier-guided generation, discussing PPLM, GeDi, DExperts, and diffusion guidance, with an explicit training-versus-decoding distinction. It also adds Constitutional Classifiers++, Constitutional AI, and broader RLHF references, while removing some earlier classifier and alignment citations.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, theoretical exposition, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Reward specification is integrated into the experiments section, and the appendices are reorganized around subgroup and judge analyses. The standalone ethics and LLM-usage statements are removed.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one column to two, with revised typography and figure placement. v2 adds an algorithm display and several result tables, expands Table 2 with subgroup rows, and relabels/resizes retained plots. The unchanged filtered-response counts are transposed from v1 Table 5 into v2 Table 10.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence by testing dependencies v1 left unexamined: prompt subgroups, alternative guards, and another judge reveal where aggregate safety–utility gains fail. The explicit theoretical assumptions and single-run disclosure also improve assessability. These gains outweigh lost protocol disclosures, although the revised reward remains unreconciled with retained scores and the conclusion overstates improvements across guards.
